confidence_notes: I did two web searches: one for the latest RBA rate and one for typical Amalfi prices, using aggregated cost-of-living sources. Those sources disagree a lot. For example, inexpensive meals ranged from about EUR 10-20 up to EUR 30, and a mid-range meal for two from about EUR 40-80 to EUR 58. Draft beer (0.5 L) was about EUR 3-5 and a cappuccino about EUR 1-3, with seated tourist prices at the high end. I raised the food and drink figures toward the top of those ranges because July is peak season and Amalfi's tourist centre adds cover charges. I converted to USD at about 1.10 USD per EUR, worked out from the RBA AUD/USD and AUD/EUR rates for 18 Nov 2026. I didn't find good direct data for cocktails or wine, so I estimated them from their usual price ratio to beer in Italian resort towns. All four accommodation prices are model estimates, not searched. They are the least certain figures because Amalfi has very few registered hostels and July prices are very high. The hostel and 1-star prices could be off by 30-40%.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on other high-end Italian coastal resorts in peak season, such as Positano, Capri, Sorrento and Cinque Terre. Amalfi is less expensive than Positano or Capri but well above the Italian average, roughly 40% higher according to one crowd-sourced index.
